newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: RUGBY UNION-IRFU TO TAKE NO ACTION AGAINST PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-IRFU TO TAKE NO ACTION AGAINST PLAYERS.

text.p: The Irish Rugby Football Union (IRFU) said on Tuesday it would take no action against three players who were the subject of complaints by France after the Five Nations game in Dublin on January 18.
The French Rugby Union Federation (FFR) sent the IRFU a videotape of incidents allegedly involving hooker Keith Wood, lock forward Paddy Johns and scrum-half Niall Hogan.
But the IRFU said in a statement it had studied the tape and found that no Irish player had committed offences which warranted disciplinary action.
The FFR last week banned prop forward Franck Tournaire from their next Five Nations game against Wales in February for stamping on Ireland hooker Allen Clarke in Dublin.
But FFR president Bernard Lapasset complained that Ireland had not followed the rules in that case and should have complained to the Five Nations championship disciplinary committee.
Lapasset said that France would not sanction players in the future if normal procedures were not followed and said Tournaire would be allowed to continue playing for his club Narbonne.
